annotations.text:
THE TILE

225 x 75 — the height is exactly a third of the width. Five fit a 1192px row with 16px gaps and three pixels to spare.

3:1 throughout. Either an uploaded wide banner filling the tile, or a generated composition: a tone-on-tone diamond lattice over a left glow, the amount in Oswald under one gold gradient clipped to the text, and a kicker beneath it. An amber chip where there is something to do, a chevron where there is not.

PROGRESS rides the bottom edge as a 3px hairline, over a soft scrim when there is artwork behind it. It is the only thing ever drawn over an uploaded image, so a personalised tile costs almost none of the design.

At this height a banner carries a wordmark and one figure. Detail belongs in the promotion copy, not the image.

Five per row and the row is a carousel: arrows beside the section link, dots underneath, more offers on the next page. On phones the same 3:1 tile runs 300 x 100, one and a peek. The promotions page uses it full width at 342 x 114 with the progress figures on a line beneath, so artwork is never written over.

The expiry bar sits above the carousel and out of the tile set. It is player state, not an offer, so it is never artwork.

The artwork here is a drawn placeholder standing in for an uploaded asset. Figures are sample values and the copy is English only.

ARTWORK UPLOAD

One wide banner per promotion at 3:1, 900 x 300 or larger. The same file is used at every width — scaled, never re-cropped — so no separate mobile asset.

Anything that is not 3:1 is refused rather than cropped.

The preview renders the real tile at real size beside the generated fallback, so removing an image has a visible consequence before it happens. Carousel position is set here too.

This needs an artwork field and alt text per promotion plus the existing upload storage. The welcome bonus is a site setting today, so it has nothing to hang an image on.

The list's old hero flag is now a real artwork column: a thumbnail when one is uploaded, a Generated tag when not.

Cashback pays at period close on these screens, not at the first hourly run that sees the threshold crossed. The numbers assume it.

The three lower screens show the content area only. The sidebar is the one drawn on the list screen above.

Balance adjustment on the player Bonuses tab sits in the admin scope. It is reachable by clerks today, with no cap and no record of who did it.
